title: 2021 USAMO Problem 5
statement:
Let \(n \geq 4\) be an integer. Find all positive real solutions to the following system of \(2n\) equations:

\begin{align*} a_{1} &=\frac{1}{a_{2 n}}+\frac{1}{a_{2}}, & a_{2}&=a_{1}+a_{3}, \\ a_{3}&=\frac{1}{a_{2}}+\frac{1}{a_{4}}, & a_{4}&=a_{3}+a_{5}, \\ a_{5}&=\frac{1}{a_{4}}+\frac{1}{a_{6}}, & a_{6}&=a_{5}+a_{7} \\ &\vdots & &\vdots \\ a_{2 n-1}&=\frac{1}{a_{2 n-2}}+\frac{1}{a_{2 n}}, & a_{2 n}&=a_{2 n-1}+a_{1} \end{align*}

§2.2 USAMO 2021/5, proposed by Mohsen Jamaali

  Problem statement

  Let n ≥ 4 be an integer. Find all positive real solutions to the following system of

The answer is that the only solution is (1, 2, 1, 2, . . . , 1, 2) which works.
  We will prove a2k is a constant sequence, at which point the result is obvious.

¶ First approach (Andrew Gu).               Apparently, with indices modulo 2n, we should have
                                                1           2      1
                                    a2k =             +        +

for every index k (this eliminates all aodd ’s). Define

                          m = min a2k               and       M = max a2k .
                                    k                                k

Look at the indices i and j achieving m and M to respectively get
                       2   1     1     2   1   1   2   2
                  m=     +    +      ≥   +   +   =   +
                       m a2i−2 a2i+2   m M     M   m M
                       2     1     1     2   1   1   2   2
                 M=      +      +      ≤   +   +   =   +   .
                       M   a2j−2 a2j+2   M   m m     m M

Together this gives m ≥ M , so m = M . That means a2i is constant as i varies, solving
the problem.

  Remark. The problem is likely intractable over C, in the sense that one gets a high-degree
  polynomial which almost certainly has many complex roots. So it seems likely that most
  solutions must involve some sort of inequality, using the fact we are over R>0 instead.
